## 固定收益開篇論述

美國與伊朗衝突再度升級，推動布蘭特原油突破每桶$95，也強化政策利率應維持限制性水準的理由。美國公債因而在7月22日連續第3個交易日下跌。2年期殖利率上升3.5個基點至4.299%，5年期上升3.4個基點至4.404%，10年期上升2.7個基點至4.656%，30年期則上升1.3個基點至5.146%。短端與中段升幅較大，使2s10s收窄0.8個基點至35.7個基點，2s30s收窄2.2個基點至84.7個基點。

油價構成最直接的通膨推力。華府擴大空襲、德黑蘭威脅進一步攻擊區域基礎設施，雙方也都未顯示準備恢復實質談判；WTI因此上漲3.34%至$87.75，布蘭特原油大漲4.79%至$95.37。風險也不再局限於受阻的荷莫茲海峽：伊朗支持的胡塞武裝表示，已準備以飛彈與無人機在曼德海峽附近發動攻擊，對能源及其他貿易的另一條航線構成威脅。

美債走勢同時反映通膨補償與投資人要求的實質報酬。10年期損益兩平通膨率上升1個基點至2.289%，10年期實質殖利率則上升1.7個基點至2.367%。不過，過去1個月10年期名目殖利率累計上升20.1個基點，實質殖利率上升18.6個基點，損益兩平通膨率僅增加1.5個基點。最新一波油價漲勢使短期通膨風險持續受到關注，但更廣泛的重新定價，主要仍由實質殖利率上升及持有利率風險所需的補償推動。

這項差異在長端尤其明顯。30年期殖利率連續第12個交易日維持在5%以上，為2007年以來最長紀錄。單日升幅較小，不代表支撐高殖利率的結構性疑慮有所紓解：美國公債市場規模已擴大至$31兆，聯邦政府每年利息支出超過$1兆，未來公共部門借款還須與龐大的AI基礎設施企業融資需求競逐長期資金。即使本輪油價帶動的債市跌勢使殖利率曲線趨平，30年期殖利率過去1個月仍上升24.7個基點。

其他市場雖承受壓力，卻未出現全面避險。標普500指數下跌0.14%，那斯達克100指數下跌0.54%；費城半導體指數在月內大幅回落後反而上漲0.44%。美元指數近乎持平，VIX下跌2.4%至16.64。地緣政治需求的作用蓋過實質殖利率上升的不利影響，黃金上漲1.5%至$4,132.10。投資級、高收益及新興市場債券基金均小幅下跌，但信用市場更重要的變化仍在個別融資案的條款與成交情況，而非市場全面失序。

## 油價延續債市跌勢，長債風險轉為結構性問題

本輪美債重新定價源於衝突再度惡化，而非新的美國經濟數據。美軍連續第11天擴大攻擊；美國總統Donald Trump則威脅，若伊朗軍方在荷莫茲海峽攻擊更多船隻，將打擊橋梁及發電廠。德黑蘭警告可能報復區域基礎設施與能源設施。外交接觸仍在繼續，但討論中的方案大致只是恢復最近一次停火破裂前已不穩定的局面。

荷莫茲海峽與曼德海峽可能同時受阻，使市場的憂慮範圍擴大。全球很大一部分能源供應通常經由荷莫茲海峽運輸；紅海南端的曼德海峽則連接通往蘇伊士運河的航運。隨著生產商設法避開受限的波斯灣航道，這條替代路線的重要性已提高；胡塞武裝準備攻擊航運，並警告為沙烏地阿拉伯港口服務的船隻，因而對該航線構成威脅。相關風險不只涉及原油產量，也涵蓋運輸時間、保險、貨運能力，以及繞開受阻區域運送燃料所需基礎設施的可靠性。

布蘭特原油收在$95.37，過去1週上漲12.27%，過去1個月上漲19.44%；WTI同期分別上漲10.24%及14.56%。這波累計漲幅發生在6月通膨數據已納入較有利的能源價格比較之後，因此後續數據可能在決策者尚未確信基礎通膨受控前，再度顯現壓力。

當日殖利率曲線熊市趨平，顯示油價帶來的近期政策疑慮在邊際上仍壓過長端既有的財政溢價。2年期殖利率上升3.5個基點，比30年期升幅多2.2個基點。這種相對走勢符合能源衝擊可能影響央行近期反應函數的情境，即使長端殖利率早已包含對供給、債務及通膨不確定性的可觀補償。

不過，30年期長債傳達的警訊更為持久。今年以來，其殖利率已有27天高於5%，約占交易日的19%；2007年則有50天。更值得注意的是，聯準會目前的基準利率比2007年低約150個基點。相對於政策利率，投資人持有期限最長的美國公債，正要求異常高的補償。

財政規模是此一要求的來源之一。美國公債未償餘額已由2007年的約$4.5兆增至$31兆；聯邦債務占GDP比重則增加逾1倍，超過100%。財政部近期雖高度依賴國庫券融資，並維持長債發行量不變，但附息債標售規模可能自2027年5月開始增加，仍帶來未來供給疑慮。

私人借款也在爭取同一批長期資金。與AI基礎設施相關的融資已超過$5,000億，使退休基金、保險公司及其他長期投資人可在主權債、高評級債與結構型專案債之間作更多選擇。政府與企業信用並非可以互換，但供給競爭會推高存續期間敏感型買方願意增持任一類債券時所要求的殖利率。

30年期實質殖利率今年已上升約50個基點，逼近3%，為2008年以來首見。這項變化顯示，當前長端壓力並非單純由通膨引發的賣壓。甚至在判斷最新能源衝擊將持續多久之前，投資人已要求更高的通膨調整後報酬，才願意承擔利率、財政與發行風險。

殖利率上升之際，美債成交量也增加。FINRA記錄的面額交易量為$1.032兆，較7月21日增加20.6%，共343,111筆交易。名目附息債交易量增加17.7%至$7,843億，TIPS交易量增加36%至$257億。超過3年、但不超過5年的券種交易尤其活躍，面額交易量增加28.4%；5年至7年期區段則增加39.5%。數據顯示，承受大部分調整的區段出現異常活躍的雙向交易，但無法判定客戶資金流向。

跨資產走勢未能為美債提供強勁的避險支撐。黃金盤中一度上漲2.1%，收盤漲幅縮至1.5%；美元變動不大，股市波動率下降。多數大型科技股在重要財報公布前走弱，晶片股則自盤中低點回升。這樣的組合使債市聚焦能源中斷的通膨後果，以及持有存續期間所要求的報酬，而不是風險資產遭到全面拋售。

## 日本與英國市場不接受通膨無虞的敘事

日本匯市與債市顯示，能源衝擊可能迫使央行重新考慮升息速度，卻無法化解長端的財政壓力。日圓一度跌至1美元兌163.24日圓，為1986年以來最弱；日本央行官員據報願意比經濟學家預期更早升息後，日圓曾短暫回升至約162.70。這波反彈隨後消退，紐約尾盤匯價接近163.15。

日本央行6月已將政策利率升至1%。多數經濟學家預期，央行將在7月31日按兵不動，12月才再次行動；但官員沒有預設路徑。若日圓疲弱與企業定價行為改變，使通膨更具持續性，他們準備提前升息。官員認為基礎通膨正接近2%目標，也觀察到與伊朗的衝突加劇後，企業更快把成本上升轉嫁給客戶。

市場預期10月前再度升息的機率，已由報導前的72%升至約84%。9月升息仍是機率較低的情境，約為32%，但MUFG策略師Lee Hardman認為日本央行可能早在9月行動。這波重新定價不只是支撐日圓的考量：官員強調貨幣政策並不以特定匯率為目標，但日圓走弱會提高進口成本，也可能強化他們正在觀察的廣泛定價行為。

直接干預只能提供短暫保護。日本當局在4月28日至5月27日期間動用¥11.73兆，日圓其後仍回到40年低點。財務大臣片山皋月再度承諾必要時將果斷行動，但反覆示警的影響力已減弱，因為推動日圓下跌的力量依舊存在，包括美國殖利率上升、龐大利差、油價上漲，以及市場對日本財政計畫的疑慮。

日本40年期公債標售則呈現較強需求，投標倍數為2.82倍，高於前次的2.702倍及過去12個月平均的2.55倍，為2025年3月以來最佳。標售後債券價格變動不大，40年期殖利率維持在3.91%附近，雖低於5月創下的4.355%紀錄，仍足以吸引壽險公司。日本保險業6月買進的超長期公債為3年來最多；明治安田生命表示，2026會計年度可能把這類部位增加最多¥1兆。

這項需求並未解決貨幣政策正常化與政府成長議程之間的衝突。首相高市早苗的計畫力求將國內儲蓄導向投資，同時又要在政府債務超過GDP 200%的國家為擴張政策籌資。德意志銀行策略師Shreyas Gopal Sachdeva認為，當局最終可能把抑制政府借款成本置於捍衛日圓之上，例如引導更多國內資金投入公債，或鼓勵日本央行重新提供支持。若透過央行購債或放慢升息來壓低殖利率，日圓可能進一步走弱；規模$1.8兆的日本政府退休金投資基金若將資金匯回，則可同時支撐債券與日圓。

英國呈現同一矛盾的不同版本。6月消費者物價通膨降至2.6%，為1年多來最低，也是連續第3次低於預期；民間部門薪資增幅亦降至2020年以來最低。這樣的組合通常會強化英國央行寬鬆預期，但貨幣市場仍反映年底前將升息近50個基點。

投資人認為這份數據反映的是過去，因為汽車燃料及食品價格下降早於最新一波油價飆升。2年期與5年期英國公債殖利率各上升約5個基點，分別至4.44%及4.63%，基準殖利率則維持在5%以上。受監管的家庭能源價格上限預計7月上調，而批發價格上升也可能在10月後反映至帳單，使市場把焦點放在下一階段的通膨，而非最新降幅。

財政政策也增添殖利率不易下降的原因。首相Andy Burnham表示，希望研究提高所得稅起徵門檻；其政府此時已因福利、支出及是否遵守現行財政規則而受到檢視。投資人歡迎John Healey出任財政大臣，但當輸入型通膨壓縮英國央行寬鬆空間之際，若紓解生活成本須增加借款，長端仍會對此保持敏感。

市場並非否定有利的通膨數據，而是判斷已實現通膨下降，尚不足以抵銷影響未來殖利率的兩股力量：短端面臨能源壓力再起，長端則存在借款規模的不確定性。因此，英國殖利率曲線未能抵銷全球持有利率風險所需報酬上升的趨勢。

## 亞洲與非洲央行持續保留匯率防線

印尼央行中止升息進程，但並未宣告匯率風險已經消退。5月及6月累計升息100個基點後，央行將BI-Rate維持在5.75%。略過半數經濟學家原本預期還會升息25個基點，因此按兵不動確實構成政策意外。公布後，印尼盾與10年期政府公債殖利率均持穩。

總裁Perry Warjiyo選擇以誘因吸引投資組合資金流入，而非再次提高國內借款成本。央行對外國投資人的避險換匯交易提供更大折價，擴大境內外市場干預，並推出以離岸人民幣計價的即期與換匯工具。Warjiyo主張，這些措施可以吸引外資並穩定匯率，無須讓政策利率再次上升的影響傳導至國內經濟。

暫停升息仍附帶鷹派條件。Warjiyo警告，衝突可能推升全球通膨、促使聯準會提前升息，並在資金轉向避險資產時帶動美元走強。能源成本上升已使印尼出現6年來首次貿易逆差；外匯存底減少，也意味油價若持續居高，印尼的緩衝將更有限。

國內情勢提供了一些等待空間。印尼央行維持2026年經濟成長率4.9%至5.7%的預測，以及1.5%至3.5%的通膨目標區間。6月整體通膨加速至3.34%，接近區間上緣，但Warjiyo預期核心通膨仍將低於3%。信用成長率為12.67%，已高於央行全年8%至12%的目標，因此也不需要透過降息提供更多支持。

進一步升息或採取非利率干預，仍是未定之數。OCBC經濟學家Lavanya Venkateswaran預期今年餘下時間將再升息75個基點；Capital Economics經濟學家Jason Tuvey則認為不會再升息。兩人的分歧取決於印尼盾能否維持穩定，以及燃料補貼能否阻止外部油價衝擊擴散為國內通膨。

其他亞洲當局已經出手干預。菲律賓披索跌至歷史低點後，該國央行賣出外幣；印度盧比逼近歷史低點時，印度央行也賣出美元。進口石油的經濟體面臨相互強化的壓力：以美元計價的能源變貴，會惡化外部收支；本幣貶值又會推高進口能源的本幣價格，並提高透過利率捍衛匯率的成本。

泰國政府公債過去1個月的走勢相反，受益於供給減少及國內通膨溫和。6月12日和平協議簽署後，10年期殖利率下跌19個基點至約2.02%，表現優於其他亞洲新興市場。會計年度計畫發債規模由約1.3兆泰銖下調至1.26兆泰銖；7月15日的10年期公債標售投標倍數達2.18倍，為近1年來該天期需求最強的一次。

支撐泰債的通膨因素早於最新一輪衝突升級，但仍有助其相對表現。6月CPI年增率由2.79%降至2.42%，低於2.7%的預測中位數。總裁Vitai Ratanakorn表示，全年通膨率可能低於央行先前預測的2.8%。風險則在外部收支：泰國是大型燃料進口國，科技產品出口快速成長，也未轉化為相應的國內生產增幅。美國銀行指出，儘管出口激增，製造業生產指數仍較上年同期下降0.8%，原因是資料中心及伺服器活動需要大量進口投入，並排擠部分傳統製造業。

南非面臨更迫切的通膨決策。6月消費者物價年增5%，高於前月的4.5%，也超過4.7%的預測中位數；運輸、住宅與公用事業、保險及金融服務的貢獻最大。數據公布後，10年期政府公債殖利率一度上升約10個基點，盤中觸及8.79%，其後回吐部分升幅。

遠期利率協議的定價已幾乎完全反映南非準備銀行將政策利率上調25個基點至7.25%。該行密切關注的2年後通膨預期則由3.6%升至3.9%。不過，升息理由並未獲得一致認同。PSG經濟學家Johann Els認為，幾乎沒有證據顯示燃料價格已對更廣泛物價產生第二輪效應；央行可以先強化鷹派訊息，同時繼續觀望。

迦納央行全體一致決議，將政策利率維持在14%。6月通膨率由3.7%升至5.3%，但仍低於央行6%至10%的目標區間。總裁Johnson Asiama表示，現行政策立場讓決策者有時間評估油價、肥料、公用事業費率及地緣政治風險。隨著能源衝擊發展，迦納因此屬於選擇維持限制性利率、而非再次升息的央行之一。

這些決策並不代表各地處於同一區域景氣循環。印尼以市場誘因替代再次升息，南非面對高於預期的通膨數據，迦納則在通膨回到目標區間前繼續維持限制性政策。共同之處在於油價壓縮了政策空間：隨著進口能源成本上升，匯率支撐、國內需求與通膨控制更難兼顧。

## AI融資考驗市場容量，強勢主權發行仍順利成交

Galaxy Digital為美國高收益債市場帶來新的大型考驗。公司計畫首次發行$35億垃圾債，為德州Helios資料中心園區提供部分資金；初步討論的殖利率約為9%。Morgan Stanley與Goldman Sachs負責安排這筆5年期債券，預計7月23日定價。

這筆融資高度依賴CoreWeave的合約收入。CoreWeave已同意以15年期合約承租運算容量，預計每年可產生逾$10億收入。專案第1期已於2026年稍早完工，第2期預計2027年啟動。工程完成10個月後，發行單位每年將償還原始本金的4%，使債權人可按計畫收回部分本金，而非完全依賴到期一次清償。

這筆交易把AI基礎設施融資進一步帶入投機級市場。今年以來，資料中心開發商已透過美國垃圾債，為特定專案籌得約$280億。Applied Digital一家子公司上月發行$15.9億債券，為CoreWeave在北達科他州的運算容量籌資；該債券其後價格約為面額的97%，殖利率接近7.88%。Galaxy擬議的發行規模與較高初始殖利率，顯示市場要求額外補償，以承擔首次發債、工程建設及租戶集中的風險。

歐洲投資人已開始限制類似融資。H.I.G. Capital支持的Polar發行創紀錄的€8億北歐債券，顯示這個條款彈性較大的市場可以容納規模異常龐大的資料中心融資；但後續發行人的空間較小。Prime Data Centers把挪威法管轄的擬議債券規模由$6億降至$5億後，仍擱置發行；Oaktree支持的Pure Data Centres則放棄擬議的€10億債券，改採銀行融資。

市場的抗拒同時反映容量與結構問題。相較資料中心專案的資金需求，北歐市場規模偏小；投資人又必須綜合合約收益、貸款價值比及未來AI需求評估借款人。部分控股公司債在結構上次順位於專案債，資金卻用於多個據點，使債權人承擔近似股權的建設與營運風險，卻無法參與股權上漲利益。Pure Data Centres的客戶也有很大部分來自雲端、電信與金融服務業，而非只依賴AI租戶。

這些挫折不代表AI信用市場已經關閉，而是顯示隨著融資管線擴大，租戶品質、結構順位、施工時程及可觀察收入的重要性都在提高。Galaxy的CoreWeave合約與分期攤還安排回應了部分疑慮，但最終定價將決定這些條件是否足以支撐一筆$35億的投機級交易。

主權債發行則顯示，即使地緣政治風險高漲，市場仍有能力承接大型高評級借款人。科威特在持續遭受伊朗飛彈與無人機攻擊之際，透過3年期、5年期及10年期美元債籌得$60億。最終條件下的訂單約達$148億，使該主權發行人得以把3個券別的定價均較初步指引收窄25個基點。

即使攻擊已損及美軍基地，以及科威特的電力與供水基礎設施，該國龐大的石油儲量、主權財富與高信用評級仍支撐發行結果。其財政狀況也已惡化：荷莫茲海峽受阻迫使科威特暫停大部分石油出口後，Goldman Sachs估計，按年率計算的赤字已接近40%。投資人把當前收入衝擊與科威特更廣泛的資產負債表承受能力區分開來，仍接受這筆大型基準債券。

尚比亞本地市場則是主權債需求分化的另一例。今年以美元計算，尚比亞克瓦查計價政府公債報酬率達36%，在Bloomberg追蹤的新興市場中表現最佳，並受惠於匯率升值20%。Citigroup策略師Katie Kironde預期，總統Hakainde Hichilema若在8月13日以壓倒性優勢連任，將吸引外資參與隨後的標售並壓低殖利率。這項預測仍以選舉結果為條件；6月26日標售的殖利率，從短端14.25%至長天期17.5%不等。

Galaxy、未能完成的北歐發行、科威特和尚比亞之間的差異，不能只以風險偏好解釋。只要交易結構、主權資產負債表或政治結果能提供充分補償，投資人仍願意供應資金；但對現金流、擔保順位或如何脫離施工風險仍難評估的大型投機專案，投資意願明顯較低。

## 再融資壓力由價格延伸至控制權

Cable One為收購Mega Broadband Investments剩餘55%股權而籌措資金，顯示契約義務如何演變成再融資角力。JPMorgan正為約$10億的第一順位債務尋找貸款人，談判圍繞接近12%的殖利率進行，為今年同類融資案擬議條件中最高者之一。

部分資金將用於向GTCR支付$4.75億至$4.95億；GTCR已於1月行使賣回選擇權。其餘資金可能透過償還或修改條款並延長到期日，處理Cable One於2028及2029年到期的債務。截至3月底，Cable One約有$30億長期債務，Moody’s已於7月把其評級調降至B2。

潛在貸款人要求加入資產與資金隔離條款，使Cable One與Mega Broadband維持分離，並阻止母公司支援被收購單位沉重的債務。此前，Mega Broadband向債權人提出的換債方案未能通過；僅34%的貸款人參與，低於擬議的近50%門檻，一個有組織的債權人團體並簽訂合作協議，以阻擋交易。

Cable One隨後警告，公司可能完成股權收購，卻不為Mega Broadband既有債務提供新的支持。S&P表示，在母公司建立實際支持紀錄前，仍會按獨立基礎評估該單位。因此，融資問題與未來現金移轉的控制權密不可分：貸款人定價時考量的不只是槓桿及寬頻業務收入減弱，也包括究竟由哪個實體承擔收購與再融資負擔。

Varta的債權人則已越過談判階段，準備拆分營運。救援協商失敗後，包括Blantyre Capital與Deutsche Bank在內的團體計畫取得這家德國電池製造商消費事業的控制權。獨立分析顯示，Varta需要約€5,000萬規模的注資，才能持續營運，但沒有任何資金來源承諾出資。

債權人團體在公司2025年重整時，已接受大幅減記並提供€6,000萬新融資；然而，營運持續惡化、亞洲製造商的競爭，以及失去Apple這個主要客戶，使當時的交易仍不足以挽救公司。Michael Tojner旗下Montana Group另行規劃透過再次重整，保留微型電池與解決方案業務；消費事業則將分拆，由債權人控制。整體公司的救援失敗，使資金缺口演變成哪些資產得以存續的取捨。

市政債投資人也正把長期實體風險轉化為當前借款成本。德州Corpus Christi最近發行10年期債券時支付60個基點的利差，相較之下，El Paso類似債券的利差為40個基點。Corpus Christi可用水源可能在2027年下半年耗盡，而重工業用戶占用水量逾半。

情勢惡化已引發評級行動。Moody’s於2025年底將Corpus Christi調降至A1；S&P在5月把其公用事業債評級下調2級至A；Fitch於6月下調3級至A-。市府官員估計，每借款$1億，評級調降會使30年期間的利息增加$375萬。

Corpus Christi正需要資金解決根本問題，借款成本卻在此時上升。市議會已批准投入$10億興建水井、再生水系統及其他基礎設施；但海水淡化廠的爭議，使一項主要的擬議供水來源延宕。Corpus Christi預計8月發行約$5億公用事業系統債券，並可能另加再融資債務。這筆發行將檢驗：當融資需求本身正是源於削弱信用的風險時，投資人是否要求進一步的懲罰性溢價。

阿根廷銀行體系面對的壓力發展較慢。當地研究機構1816 Economía & Estrategia估計，超過四分之一的借款人已不再符合授信資格。薪資疲弱、勞動市場低迷，已推升逾期還款，促使銀行收緊授信標準，也限制家庭信貸對經濟復甦的貢獻。

央行官員認為，隨著利率穩定，不良貸款可能已於6月觸頂；但銀行業者與經濟學家預期，改善只會逐步發生。通膨下降後，消費信貸快速擴張，銀行也不再以對政府放款為主要業務，因而暴露於承銷風險。數十年的金融壓抑，以及債務實質價值快速遭通膨侵蝕，過去曾掩蓋這些風險。

自總統Javier Milei上任以來，阿根廷信貸規模雖已增加近1倍，但仍僅約占GDP的12%，巴西則約為80%。長期而言，阿根廷仍有很大的信貸擴張空間，但這項轉型是在缺乏成熟借款紀錄及廣泛家庭資產負債表韌性的情況下進行。Moody’s調升主權評級後，也以經濟復甦與通膨下降為由，調高阿根廷最大型銀行的評級；不過，當前不良貸款增加顯示，主權穩定與家庭信用品質可能依不同時程改善。

綜合這些案例，高殖利率不只是壓低債券價格，也在改變治理、擔保品安排及企業能否存續。Cable One的貸款人要求為現金與資產設置屏障；Varta的債權人準備拆分公司；Corpus Christi為必要基礎設施籌資時面臨更高成本；阿根廷銀行則在舊貸款惡化之際限制新增信用。共同限制在於，無法延後融資需求的借款人，所剩迴旋空間正不斷縮小。

## 後續市場意義

南非準備銀行7月23日的決策，將顯示高於預期的通膨，以及上升的2年期通膨預期，是否足以促成升息25個基點至7.25%。若升息，將驗證遠期利率協議幾乎已完全反映的調整；若按兵不動但提出更強硬的指引，則表示決策者仍認為第二輪效應證據不足，無須立即行動。

Galaxy Digital預計同日定價，是近期最明確的一項測試，可衡量美國投機級市場對AI基礎設施融資的需求。關鍵條件包括最終規模與殖利率、投資人如何評價CoreWeave的15年期租約，以及定期償還本金能否充分抵銷施工與租戶集中風險，從而支撐一筆$35億的首次發行。順利成交只會為這項專案建立市場成交水準，不會消除北歐交易遭放棄所揭示的容量限制。

美國6月新屋銷售將於7月24日公布，接著是7月27日的耐久財訂單初值，以及7月28日的先期經濟指標。房市數據將檢驗偏高的美債與房貸利率造成多少壓抑；耐久財及貿易相關指標則會顯示，企業需求是否仍強到足以支撐高實質殖利率。這組數據將有助判斷，在最新能源漲勢尚未完全反映於通膨數據前，當前金融情勢是否已在拖慢經濟活動。

聯邦公開市場委員會將於7月28至29日開會，屆時10年期殖利率的實質與通膨補償兩個部分均在上升，油價也已高於$95。眼前問題是，官員會回應能源價格可能產生的傳導，還是等待影響擴大的證據。對殖利率曲線而言，更大的問題是：當財政與企業供給已推高長期借款成本時，聯準會是否會把高實質殖利率視為足夠的緊縮力量。

日本央行7月31日會議，將檢驗官員準備早於經濟學家偏好的12月時程收緊政策之報導。市場普遍預期維持利率不變，但央行如何描述基礎通膨、企業定價行為及日圓貶值的傳導，將決定市場所反映的10月前升息機率約84%能否維持。40年期公債標售顯示，較高殖利率可以吸引國內買家；但在政府力求控制融資成本之際，貨幣緊縮還能推進多遠，仍未得到解答。

8月有兩項性質不同的市場融資測試。Corpus Christi計畫發行約$5億公用事業債，為水務基礎設施籌資，市政債投資人必須同時為氣候相關信用問題，以及用來緩解該問題的工程定價。尚比亞8月13日的選舉，則將決定Citigroup所預期的外資重返後續本地公債標售，是否有足夠明確的政治結果作為依據。

固定收益市場的核心問題，正由油價衝擊是否促成再一次升息，擴展至更廣的層面。短端正在重新反映央行可能必須維持限制性政策；長天期市場則須吸收主權赤字及日益增加的基礎設施債務供給。科威特證明借款人仍能籌得大額資金，但北歐發行失敗、Cable One的融資談判及Varta拆分都顯示，資本正依交易結構、擔保品與資產負債表承受能力作出嚴格區別。

overall_summary.headline: 油價衝擊強化限制性利率與存續期間壓力，美債下跌
overall_summary.session_narrative:
美國與伊朗衝突升級、油價延續漲勢，美國公債連續第3個交易日下跌。2年期殖利率上升3.5個基點至4.299%，5年期上升3.4個基點至4.404%，10年期上升2.7個基點至4.656%，30年期上升1.3個基點至5.146%。短端與中段升幅較大，使2s10s收窄至35.7個基點，2s30s收窄至84.7個基點。

華府擴大攻擊、德黑蘭威脅區域基礎設施，胡塞武裝也準備在曼德海峽附近發動攻擊，帶動布蘭特原油上漲4.79%至$95.37。兩條主要貿易航線均可能受阻，提高能源價格、貨運、保險及通膨壓力再起時點的風險。

本輪賣壓並非單純的通膨交易。10年期實質殖利率上升1.7個基點，損益兩平通膨率則上升1個基點；過去1個月10年期名目殖利率的漲幅，也大多來自實質殖利率。30年期殖利率連續第12個交易日維持在5%以上，財政借款與逾$5,000億的AI相關融資正競逐長期資金。股市小幅走弱、美元近乎持平、波動率下降，未能為美債提供多少避險支撐。信用市場仍然開放，但選擇性提高：強勢主權發行順利成交，大型AI專案及財務承壓的再融資案則在結構、擔保品與償債能力方面受到更嚴格檢視。

## Opening Fixed-Income Thesis

Treasuries fell for a third session on July 22 as another escalation in the U.S.-Iran conflict pushed Brent crude above $95 a barrel and strengthened the case for keeping policy rates restrictive. The 2-year yield rose 3.5 basis points to 4.299%, the 5-year increased 3.4 basis points to 4.404%, the 10-year climbed 2.7 basis points to 4.656%, and the 30-year added 1.3 basis points to 5.146%. The larger increases through the front and intermediate sectors narrowed 2s10s by 0.8 basis point to 35.7 basis points and 2s30s by 2.2 basis points to 84.7 basis points.

Oil supplied the immediate inflation impulse. WTI gained 3.34% to $87.75 and Brent surged 4.79% to $95.37 after Washington widened its airstrikes, Tehran threatened further attacks on regional infrastructure, and neither side showed readiness to resume substantive negotiations. The risk also extended beyond the impaired Strait of Hormuz: Iran-backed Houthi forces said they had prepared missiles and drones for attacks near the Bab el-Mandeb, threatening a second route for energy and other trade.

The Treasury move reflected both inflation compensation and the required real return. The 10-year breakeven rate increased 1 basis point to 2.289%, while the 10-year real yield rose 1.7 basis points to 2.367%. Over the past month, however, the 10-year nominal yield has climbed 20.1 basis points and the real yield 18.6 basis points, against only a 1.5-basis-point increase in the breakeven. The latest oil surge kept near-term inflation risk in view, but the broader repricing still depended principally on higher real yields and compensation for holding duration.

That distinction was especially visible at the long end. The 30-year yield remained above 5% for a 12th consecutive trading session, the longest run since 2007. Its smaller daily increase did not indicate relief from the structural concerns keeping it elevated: the Treasury market has expanded to $31 trillion, annual federal interest costs exceed $1 trillion, and prospective public borrowing is competing with a large pipeline of corporate financing for artificial-intelligence infrastructure. The long bond’s yield has risen 24.7 basis points over a month even as the curve flattened during the latest oil-driven selloff.

Other markets showed pressure without a generalized flight from risk. The S&P 500 declined 0.14% and the Nasdaq 100 lost 0.54%, while the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index gained 0.44% after a steep monthly retreat. The dollar index was nearly unchanged, and the VIX fell 2.4% to 16.64. Gold rose 1.5% to $4,132.10 as geopolitical demand outweighed the drag from higher real yields. Investment-grade, high-yield and emerging-market bond funds all declined modestly, leaving the more consequential credit developments in the terms and execution of individual financings rather than a broad market rupture.

## Oil Extends the Selloff as Long-Bond Risk Becomes Structural

The repricing in Treasuries followed another deterioration in the conflict rather than a fresh U.S. economic release. American forces widened their strikes for an 11th consecutive day, while President Donald Trump threatened attacks on bridges and power plants if Iran’s military targeted more ships in the Strait of Hormuz. Tehran warned that it could retaliate against regional infrastructure and energy facilities. Diplomatic contacts continued, but the proposals under discussion amounted largely to restoring the unstable conditions that existed before the latest ceasefire broke down.

The possibility of disruption at both Hormuz and the Bab el-Mandeb broadened the market’s concern. Hormuz ordinarily carries a large share of global energy supplies, while the narrow passage at the southern end of the Red Sea connects traffic to the Suez Canal. Houthi preparations to attack shipping and their warning against vessels serving Saudi ports threatened the route that had become more important as producers sought alternatives to constrained Gulf passage. The resulting risk was not limited to crude production; it encompassed transport time, insurance, freight capacity and the reliability of the infrastructure needed to move fuel around the disruption.

Brent’s close at $95.37 left it 12.27% higher over a week and 19.44% higher over a month. WTI was up 10.24% over a week and 14.56% over a month. The cumulative rise has occurred after the June inflation data captured a more favorable energy comparison, increasing the risk that subsequent readings will show renewed pressure before policymakers can be confident that underlying inflation is contained.

The day’s bearish flattening showed that this immediate policy concern remained more powerful at the margin than the long end’s existing fiscal premium. The 2-year yield’s 3.5-basis-point increase exceeded the 30-year move by 2.2 basis points. That relationship is consistent with an energy shock that can influence the near-term reaction function even while long yields already embed substantial compensation for supply, debt and inflation uncertainty.

The long bond nevertheless carried the session’s more persistent warning. It has traded above 5% on 27 days this year, or about 19% of sessions, compared with 50 days during 2007. The comparison is more striking because the Federal Reserve’s benchmark rate is now about 150 basis points below its 2007 level. Investors are therefore demanding unusually high compensation to hold the longest Treasury maturity relative to the policy rate.

Fiscal scale is one source of that demand. Treasury debt outstanding has risen from about $4.5 trillion in 2007 to $31 trillion, while federal debt has more than doubled relative to gross domestic product to exceed 100%. The prospect that coupon-auction sizes may begin increasing by May 2027 adds a future supply question even though Treasury has recently relied heavily on bills and kept long-bond issuance steady.

Private borrowing is competing for the same long-duration capital. More than $500 billion of financing has been associated with AI infrastructure, giving pensions, insurers and other long-horizon investors a wider menu of sovereign, high-grade and structured project debt. That does not make government and corporate credit interchangeable, but it raises the yield at which duration-sensitive buyers are willing to absorb another increment of either.

The 30-year real yield has risen about 50 basis points this year toward 3%, a level last reached in 2008. That move distinguishes the current long-end pressure from an inflation-only selloff. Investors are seeking a larger inflation-adjusted return for bearing duration, fiscal and issuance risk even before determining how persistent the latest energy shock will be.

Treasury turnover increased as yields rose. FINRA recorded $1.032 trillion of par activity, 20.6% more than on July 21, across 343,111 trades. Nominal-coupon activity rose 17.7% to $784.3 billion, while TIPS volume increased 36% to $25.7 billion. Trading was particularly active in maturities longer than 3 years and no more than 5 years, where par volume increased 28.4%, and in the 5- to 7-year sector, where it rose 39.5%. The figures show unusually heavy two-way activity in the sectors bearing much of the adjustment, without identifying the direction of customer flow.

The cross-asset response did not provide Treasuries with a strong haven offset. Gold advanced as much as 2.1% intraday before closing 1.5% higher, but the dollar was little changed and equity volatility declined. Chipmakers recovered from session lows even as most large technology shares weakened before major earnings announcements. The combination left the bond market focused on the inflation consequences of energy disruption and the price required to own duration, rather than on a broad liquidation of risky assets.

## Japan and Britain Resist Benign Inflation Narratives

Japan’s currency and bond markets showed how an energy shock can force a central bank to reconsider the pace of tightening without resolving long-end fiscal pressure. The yen fell to 163.24 per dollar, its weakest level since 1986, before briefly strengthening to about 162.70 after reports that Bank of Japan officials were open to increasing rates sooner than economists expected. The rebound faded, and the currency traded near 163.15 late in New York.

The BOJ raised its policy rate to 1% in June, and most economists expect it to hold on July 31 before moving again in December. Officials have no preset course, however, and are prepared to act earlier if currency weakness and changing corporate pricing behavior make inflation more persistent. They see underlying inflation approaching the 2% target and evidence that companies have become quicker to pass higher costs to customers since the conflict with Iran intensified.

Markets increased the implied probability of another rate rise by October to about 84%, from 72% before the report. A September increase remained a less likely outcome at roughly 32%, although MUFG strategist Lee Hardman said the BOJ could move that soon. The repricing reflects more than an attempt to support the yen: officials maintain that monetary policy does not target a particular exchange rate, but a weaker currency raises import costs and can reinforce the broader price-setting behavior they are monitoring.

Direct intervention has offered only temporary protection. Japanese authorities spent ¥11.73 trillion between April 28 and May 27, yet the yen subsequently returned to a 4-decade low. Finance Minister Satsuki Katayama again promised bold action if necessary, but repeated warnings have lost some influence because the forces behind the decline remain intact: higher U.S. yields, a wide interest-rate differential, rising oil costs and concern about Japan’s fiscal plans.

The domestic bond market did produce stronger demand at a 40-year auction. The sale drew bids equal to 2.82 times the amount offered, up from 2.702 at the previous auction and above the 12-month average of 2.55. It was the strongest demand since March 2025. Bonds changed little after the result, and the 40-year yield remained near 3.91%, below its May record of 4.355% but high enough to attract life insurers. Japanese insurers bought the most super-long government bonds in 3 years in June, and Meiji Yasuda Life said it could increase such holdings by as much as ¥1 trillion during fiscal 2026.

That demand does not settle the conflict between monetary normalization and the government’s growth agenda. Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi’s program seeks to mobilize domestic savings for investment while financing expansionary policies in a country whose debt exceeds 200% of GDP. Deutsche Bank strategist Shreyas Gopal Sachdeva argued that the authorities may eventually place greater weight on restraining government borrowing costs than defending the currency, potentially by directing more domestic capital toward government bonds or encouraging renewed BOJ support. Measures that suppress yields through central-bank purchases or slower tightening would risk further yen weakness; repatriation by the $1.8 trillion Government Pension Investment Fund could support both bonds and the currency.

Britain presented a different version of the same tension. June consumer-price inflation slowed to 2.6%, the lowest in more than a year and the third consecutive downside surprise. Private-sector wage growth also fell to its slowest pace since 2020. Ordinarily that combination would strengthen expectations for Bank of England easing. Instead, money markets continued to price almost 50 basis points of rate increases by year-end.

Investors treated the release as backward-looking because lower motor-fuel and food prices preceded the latest oil surge. The 2-year and 5-year gilt yields each rose about 5 basis points, to 4.44% and 4.63%, respectively, while benchmark yields remained above 5%. The expected July increase in the regulated household energy-price cap and the possibility that higher wholesale prices will feed into bills after October left the market focused on the next inflation phase rather than the latest decline.

Fiscal policy added another source of resistance to lower yields. Prime Minister Andy Burnham said he wanted to examine raising the threshold at which income tax begins, while his government was already facing scrutiny over welfare, spending and its commitment to existing fiscal rules. Investors welcomed John Healey’s appointment as chancellor, but the longer end remained sensitive to the risk that cost-of-living relief would require more borrowing just as imported inflation reduced the BOE’s room for accommodation.

The result was not a rejection of the favorable inflation data. It was a judgment that lower realized inflation had not yet neutralized the two forces shaping prospective yields: renewed energy pressure at the front end and uncertainty over borrowing at the long end. Britain’s curve therefore offered no offset to the global increase in the required return on duration.

## Asian and African Central Banks Keep Currency Defense in Play

Bank Indonesia interrupted its tightening campaign but did not declare the currency risk resolved. It left the BI-Rate at 5.75% after increasing it by a cumulative 100 basis points in May and June. A narrow majority of economists had expected another 25-basis-point rise, making the hold a genuine policy surprise. The rupiah and 10-year government-bond yield were steady after the announcement.

Governor Perry Warjiyo chose incentives for portfolio inflows over another increase in domestic borrowing costs. The central bank offered foreign investors larger discounts on hedging swaps, expanded offshore and onshore intervention, and introduced spot and swap instruments denominated in offshore yuan. Warjiyo argued that these measures could attract foreign capital and stabilize the currency without transmitting another policy-rate increase through the domestic economy.

The pause retained a hawkish condition. Warjiyo warned that the conflict could accelerate global inflation, cause the Fed to raise rates sooner and strengthen the dollar as capital moved toward havens. Indonesia has already recorded its first trade deficit in 6 years as energy costs rose, and depleted foreign-exchange reserves leave less protection if oil remains elevated.

Domestic conditions allowed some room to wait. Bank Indonesia maintained its 2026 growth forecast at 4.9% to 5.7% and its inflation target range of 1.5% to 3.5%. Headline inflation accelerated to 3.34% in June, near the upper end of that band, but Warjiyo expects core inflation to remain below 3%. Credit growth was 12.67%, above the central bank’s full-year goal of 8% to 12%, reducing the need for additional support through lower rates.

The choice between further tightening and non-rate intervention remains open. OCBC economist Lavanya Venkateswaran expects another 75 basis points of increases over the rest of the year, while Capital Economics economist Jason Tuvey expects no more hikes. Their disagreement turns on whether the rupiah remains stable and subsidized fuel prevents the external oil shock from broadening into domestic inflation.

Other Asian authorities were already intervening. The Philippine central bank sold foreign currency after the peso reached a record low, and the Reserve Bank of India sold dollars as the rupee approached its weakest level. Oil-importing economies face a reinforcing pressure: more expensive dollar-denominated energy worsens their external balances, while depreciation raises the local-currency price of those imports and increases the cost of defending exchange rates through interest rates.

Thailand’s government bonds moved in the opposite direction over the preceding month, supported by reduced supply and subdued domestic inflation. The 10-year yield fell 19 basis points to about 2.02% after the June 12 peace agreement, outperforming emerging Asian peers. Planned fiscal-year issuance was reduced to about 1.26 trillion baht from 1.3 trillion baht, while a July 15 sale of 10-year debt drew bids equal to 2.18 times the amount offered, the strongest demand for that maturity in almost a year.

The inflation support for Thai bonds predates the latest escalation but remains relevant to their relative performance. Annual CPI slowed to 2.42% in June from 2.79%, below the 2.7% median forecast. Governor Vitai Ratanakorn said inflation was likely to undershoot the central bank’s previous 2.8% full-year projection. The vulnerability lies in the external accounts: Thailand is a large fuel importer, and rapid growth in technology exports has not translated into comparable domestic production. Bank of America noted that the manufacturing-production index was 0.8% lower than a year earlier even as exports surged because data-center and server activity required substantial imported inputs and displaced parts of legacy manufacturing.

South Africa faced a more immediate inflation decision. Consumer prices rose 5% from a year earlier in June, accelerating from 4.5% and exceeding the 4.7% median estimate. Transport, housing and utilities, insurance and financial services made the largest contributions. The 10-year government yield rose about 10 basis points after the release to an intraday high of 8.79% before recovering part of the move.

Forward-rate agreements almost fully priced a 25-basis-point increase in the South African Reserve Bank’s policy rate to 7.25%. Inflation expectations 2 years ahead, a measure watched closely by the bank, increased to 3.9% from 3.6%. The case for tightening was not unanimous: PSG economist Johann Els argued that there was little evidence of second-round effects from fuel into broader prices and that the bank could instead reinforce a hawkish message while waiting.

Ghana kept its policy rate at 14% by a unanimous vote. Inflation rose to 5.3% in June from 3.7%, but remained below the central bank’s 6% to 10% target band. Governor Johnson Asiama said the existing stance gave policymakers time to assess oil, fertilizer, utility-tariff and geopolitical risks. The decision placed Ghana with the group of central banks choosing a restrictive hold rather than a fresh increase as the energy shock develops.

These decisions were not expressions of a common regional cycle. Indonesia substituted market incentives for another hike, South Africa confronted an upside data surprise, and Ghana retained restraint before inflation returned to target. What connected them was the narrowing room created by oil: currency support, domestic demand and inflation control all became harder to balance as the cost of imported energy rose.

## AI Borrowing Tests Capacity While Strong Sovereigns Still Clear

The U.S. high-yield market faced a large new test from Galaxy Digital. The company planned a debut $3.5 billion junk-bond sale to finance part of its Helios data-center campus in Texas, with initial discussions centered on a yield of about 9%. Morgan Stanley and Goldman Sachs were arranging the 5-year issue for expected pricing on July 23.

The financing depends heavily on contracted revenue from CoreWeave, which has agreed to lease computing capacity under 15-year contracts expected to generate more than $1 billion annually. The first project phase was completed earlier in 2026, and the second is expected to begin in 2027. The issuing unit would repay 4% of original principal each year beginning 10 months after construction is completed, giving creditors some scheduled amortization rather than relying entirely on a bullet maturity.

The transaction extends AI infrastructure borrowing into speculative-grade markets. Data-center developers have raised about $28 billion from U.S. junk bonds this year for specific projects. An Applied Digital subsidiary sold $1.59 billion last month to fund CoreWeave capacity in North Dakota; that bond later traded around 97 cents on the dollar for a yield near 7.88%. Galaxy’s proposed size and higher initial yield show the additional compensation sought for a debut issuer, construction exposure and concentrated tenant economics.

European investors had already begun imposing limits on similar borrowing. H.I.G. Capital-backed Polar sold a record €800 million Nordic bond, demonstrating that the flexible market could accommodate unusually large data-center financing. Subsequent issuers found less room. Prime Data Centers shelved a Norwegian-law bond after reducing its planned size to $500 million from $600 million, while Oaktree-backed Pure Data Centres abandoned a proposed €1 billion issue in favor of bank financing.

The resistance reflected both capacity and structure. The Nordic market is small relative to the capital needs of data-center projects, and investors were being asked to evaluate borrowers through a mixture of contracted earnings, loan-to-value ratios and prospective AI demand. Some holding-company bonds were structurally subordinated to project debt while funding multiple sites, leaving creditors exposed to equity-like execution risk without equity participation in the upside. Pure Data Centres also relied substantially on cloud, telecommunications and financial-services customers rather than solely on AI tenants.

These setbacks did not amount to a closure of AI credit. They established that tenant quality, structural seniority, construction timing and observable revenue matter more as the borrowing pipeline grows. Galaxy’s CoreWeave contracts and amortization schedule address parts of that concern, but its pricing will determine whether they are sufficient for a $3.5 billion speculative-grade transaction.

Sovereign issuance showed that investors still had capacity for large, highly rated borrowers despite geopolitical danger. Kuwait raised $6 billion through 3-, 5- and 10-year dollar bonds while the country was enduring repeated Iranian missile and drone attacks. Orders reached about $14.8 billion at final terms, allowing the sovereign to tighten pricing by 25 basis points across all 3 tranches from initial indications.

The result reflected Kuwait’s large oil reserves, sovereign wealth and high credit rating, even as attacks damaged U.S. bases and Kuwaiti power and water infrastructure. Its fiscal position has also deteriorated: Goldman Sachs estimated that the deficit had reached almost 40% on an annualized basis after disruption through Hormuz forced the suspension of most oil exports. Investors distinguished that current revenue shock from Kuwait’s broader balance-sheet capacity and accepted a large benchmark sale.

Zambia’s local market supplied another example of differentiated sovereign demand. Kwacha-denominated government bonds returned 36% in dollar terms this year, the strongest performance among emerging markets tracked by Bloomberg, aided by a 20% currency appreciation. Citigroup strategist Katie Kironde expects a decisive reelection victory for President Hakainde Hichilema on August 13 to attract foreign investors to the following auction and pull yields lower. The forecast remains conditional on the vote; yields at the June 26 auction ranged from 14.25% at the short end to 17.5% on longer maturities.

The contrast among Galaxy, the failed Nordic offerings, Kuwait and Zambia was not simply one of risk appetite. Investors were willing to provide capital where the structure, sovereign balance sheet or political outcome offered sufficient compensation. They were less willing to fund large speculative projects whose cash flows, collateral position or exit from construction risk remained difficult to assess.

## Refinancing Stress Moves from Price to Control

Cable One’s effort to finance its purchase of the remaining 55% of Mega Broadband Investments showed how a contractual obligation can turn into a refinancing contest. JPMorgan was seeking lenders for roughly $1 billion of first-lien debt, with negotiations centered on a yield near 12%, among the highest proposed for such financing this year.

Part of the proceeds would fund a $475 million to $495 million payment to GTCR, which exercised a put option in January. The rest would address Cable One debt due in 2028 and 2029 through a possible repayment or an amend-and-extend transaction. Cable One had about $3 billion of long-term debt at the end of March and was downgraded by Moody’s to B2 in July.

Prospective lenders were seeking ring-fencing provisions to keep Cable One and Mega Broadband separate and prevent the parent from supporting the acquired unit’s heavy debt load. That demand followed the failure of an exchange offered to Mega Broadband creditors. Only 34% of lenders participated, short of a proposed threshold near 50%, and an organized creditor group entered a cooperation agreement to block the transaction.

Cable One subsequently warned that it might complete the equity purchase without providing new support to Mega Broadband’s existing debt. S&P said it would continue assessing the unit on a stand-alone basis until the parent established a record of support. The financing question is therefore inseparable from control over future cash transfers: lenders are pricing not only leverage and weaker broadband revenue, but also which entity will bear the acquisition and refinancing burden.

Varta’s creditors moved beyond negotiations toward an operational breakup. A group including Blantyre Capital and Deutsche Bank planned to take control of the German battery maker’s consumer division after rescue discussions failed. Independent analysis indicated that Varta needed a mid-double-digit-million-euro injection to operate sustainably, but no source committed the funds.

The creditor group had already accepted a substantial haircut and provided €60 million of new financing during the company’s 2025 restructuring. Continued deterioration, competition from Asian manufacturers and the loss of Apple as a major customer left that transaction insufficient. Michael Tojner’s Montana Group separately planned to preserve the microbattery and solutions operations through another restructuring, while the consumer business would be carved out under creditor control. The failure of a whole-company rescue converted a financing shortfall into decisions over which assets could survive.

Municipal investors were also translating a long-term physical risk into current borrowing costs. Corpus Christi, Texas, paid a spread of 60 basis points on a recent 10-year sale, compared with 40 basis points for a similar El Paso bond. The city may exhaust its usable water supply in the second half of 2027, and heavy industrial users account for more than half of consumption.

The deterioration has already produced rating action. Moody’s lowered Corpus Christi to A1 in late 2025, S&P cut its utility debt by 2 notches to A in May, and Fitch reduced it by 3 notches to A- in June. City officials estimate that the downgrade adds $3.75 million of interest over 30 years for each $100 million borrowed.

The higher cost arrives as Corpus Christi needs capital to address the underlying problem. The city council approved $1 billion of wells, recycled-water systems and other infrastructure, while debate over a seawater-desalination plant delayed a major proposed source of supply. Corpus Christi expects to sell about $500 million of utility-system bonds in August, possibly with additional refinancing debt. The sale will test whether investors require a further penalty when the financing need itself arises from the risk weakening the credit.

Argentina’s banking system presented a slower-moving form of stress. Local research firm 1816 Economía & Estrategia estimated that more than a quarter of borrowers were no longer considered creditworthy. Weak wages and a soft labor market have lifted delinquencies, caused banks to tighten standards and limited the household-credit contribution to the economic recovery.

Central-bank officials believe bad loans may have peaked in June as interest rates stabilized, but bankers and economists expect only gradual improvement. Consumer credit expanded rapidly as inflation fell and banks shifted away from lending primarily to the government, exposing institutions to underwriting risks that had been obscured by decades of financial repression and rapidly eroding real debt burdens.

Credit in Argentina remains only about 12% of GDP, despite nearly doubling since President Javier Milei took office, compared with roughly 80% in Brazil. That leaves substantial long-run room for expansion but also means the transition is occurring without mature borrower histories or broad household balance-sheet resilience. Moody’s upgraded the largest Argentine banks after raising the sovereign rating, citing economic recovery and falling inflation, yet the present increase in bad loans shows that sovereign stabilization and household credit quality can improve on different timetables.

Across these cases, high yields were not merely reducing bond prices. They were altering governance, collateral and corporate survival. Cable One’s lenders sought barriers around cash and assets, Varta’s creditors prepared to divide the company, Corpus Christi faced a higher cost for funding essential infrastructure, and Argentine banks restricted new credit as old loans weakened. The common constraint was the shrinking margin for borrowers whose financing needs could not be deferred.

## Forward Market Significance

The July 23 South African Reserve Bank decision will show whether the upside inflation surprise and higher 2-year expectations are sufficient to produce a 25-basis-point increase to 7.25%. A hike would validate the nearly complete adjustment in forward-rate agreements. A hold accompanied by tougher guidance would indicate that policymakers still see insufficient second-round evidence to act immediately.

Galaxy Digital’s expected pricing the same day is the clearest near-term test of U.S. speculative-grade demand for AI infrastructure. The relevant terms are the final size and yield, the value assigned to the 15-year CoreWeave leases, and whether scheduled principal repayment offsets enough construction and tenant concentration risk to support a $3.5 billion debut. Successful execution would establish a clearing level for this project, not remove the capacity constraints exposed by the abandoned Nordic deals.

June U.S. new-home sales arrive July 24, followed by advance durable-goods orders on July 27 and advance economic indicators on July 28. Housing will test the restraint imposed by elevated Treasury and mortgage rates, while durable goods and the trade-related indicators will show whether business demand remains firm enough to sustain high real yields. The sequence will help determine whether current financial conditions are slowing activity before the latest energy rise appears fully in inflation data.

The Federal Open Market Committee meets July 28–29 with both components of the 10-year yield moving higher and oil above $95. The immediate question is whether officials respond to the prospective pass-through from energy or wait for evidence that it is broadening. The larger issue for the curve is whether the Fed treats high real yields as sufficient restraint when long-duration borrowing costs are already elevated by fiscal and corporate supply.

The BOJ’s July 31 meeting will test the report that officials are prepared to tighten earlier than the December timetable favored by economists. A hold is widely expected, but the description of underlying inflation, company pricing behavior and yen pass-through will determine whether the market’s roughly 84% probability of an increase by October is durable. The 40-year auction showed that higher yields can attract domestic buyers; it did not resolve how far monetary tightening can proceed while the government seeks to contain funding costs.

August brings two distinct market-access tests. Corpus Christi plans to sell about $500 million of utility debt for water infrastructure, forcing municipal investors to price a climate-related credit problem and the projects intended to mitigate it at the same time. Zambia’s August 13 election will determine whether Citigroup’s expectation of renewed foreign demand at the subsequent local-bond auction rests on a sufficiently decisive political result.

The central fixed-income question is becoming broader than whether the oil shock produces another policy increase. Front ends are repricing the possibility that central banks must remain restrictive, while long maturities face sovereign deficits and a growing volume of infrastructure debt. Borrowers can still raise large amounts, as Kuwait demonstrated, but the failed Nordic offerings, Cable One negotiations and Varta breakup show that capital is discriminating sharply by structure, collateral and balance-sheet capacity.

overall_summary.headline: Treasuries fall as the oil shock reinforces restrictive-rate and duration pressure
overall_summary.session_narrative:
Treasuries fell for a third session as the U.S.-Iran conflict escalated and oil extended its surge. The 2-year yield rose 3.5 basis points to 4.299%, the 5-year increased 3.4 basis points to 4.404%, the 10-year climbed 2.7 basis points to 4.656%, and the 30-year added 1.3 basis points to 5.146%. The larger front- and intermediate-sector moves narrowed 2s10s to 35.7 basis points and 2s30s to 84.7 basis points.

Brent gained 4.79% to $95.37 after Washington widened its strikes, Tehran threatened regional infrastructure and Houthi forces prepared attacks near the Bab el-Mandeb. The prospect of disruption across two major trade routes raised risks to energy prices, freight, insurance and the timing of renewed inflation pressure.

The selloff was not solely an inflation trade. The 10-year real yield rose 1.7 basis points, compared with a 1-basis-point increase in the breakeven rate, and real yields account for most of the 10-year nominal yield's rise over the past month. The 30-year yield remained above 5% for a 12th consecutive session as fiscal borrowing and more than $500 billion of AI-related financing competed for long-duration capital. Equities weakened modestly, the dollar was nearly unchanged and volatility declined, offering Treasuries little haven support. Credit remained open but selective, with strong sovereign issuance clearing while large AI projects and stressed refinancings faced sharper scrutiny of structure, collateral and repayment capacity.
overall_summary.summary: Treasury yields rose and curves flattened as the widening U.S.-Iran conflict drove Brent above $95, lifting near-term inflation risk while high real yields, fiscal supply and competing corporate borrowing kept long-duration pressure elevated.
